label: Hospitality, tourism and cruise
description: The organizations that look after guests away from home: a cruise line with its ships and shoreside teams, a hotel or resort, and a destination tourism board. Plans and products: the ship's outbreak prevention and response plan and medical log, the safety management system, the muster and passenger accounting list, the in-house guest list, the hurricane plan, reports to the CDC Vessel Sanitation Program and the quarantine station, alleged crime reports to the FBI and Coast Guard, and guest letters and holding statements. Three variants share one profile: cruise line (ship and shoreside), hotel or resort (which borrows the lodging roles and systems of the commercial facilities profile), and tourism board. Port operations on the shore side belong to the port and maritime profile; stadiums and events belong to the stadium and venue profile.

vocabulary.frontline: cabin stewards, front desk agents, housekeepers, security officers, medical staff, food and beverage staff, shuttle drivers
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the ship's bridge and safety center, the hotel's command post, or the shoreside operations center

addedThreatFamilies.label: Gastroenteritis outbreak at sea or in a property
addedThreatFamilies.description: Cases of acute gastroenteritis (usually norovirus) climb in the medical log of a ship, or among guests and staff of a resort; reports, isolation, cleaning, guest messages and the boarding decision for the next voyage follow the counts.

phaseArc.title: First cluster in the medical log
phaseArc.goal: Players see the first cases and decide whether this is a cluster and what to start now.
beats: The medical log shows several cases from one deck within a day
The environmental health officer asks whether a common meal is involved
The hotel director asks whether to keep buffets open

phaseArc.title: Threshold crossed
phaseArc.goal: Counts reach 2 percent and then 3 percent of passengers or crew; reports are due, and the ship is days from a US port.
beats: A special report is due at 2 percent and again at 3 percent
The 24-hour report point to the quarantine station approaches
Crew cases include food handlers

phaseArc.title: Response, reports and guest communication
phaseArc.goal: Isolation, cleaning, specimens and the cumulative report run while guests and families ask questions.
beats: Passengers ask for refunds and itinerary changes
A guest posts a video of the infirmary queue
The ship asks the shoreside team whether to skip a port

phaseArc.title: Arrival and the next voyage
phaseArc.goal: Port health boards or meets the ship, and the line decides whether the next voyage boards on time.
beats: The 4-hour update report changes the count
The port authority asks about cleaning in the terminal
The boarding decision memo is due before embarkation opens

phaseArc.title: Investigation and close-out
phaseArc.goal: Counts fall, the cause is discussed and the hot wash records what held and what slipped.
beats: Laboratory results arrive
Compensation and claims questions begin
The outbreak response plan is reviewed

decisionPointExamples: report the 2 percent count by special report and call now, or wait one more shift of the medical log and risk a late report
skip the next port to shorten the ship's exposure, or keep the itinerary to protect guest plans
delay boarding of the next voyage until the terminal and ship are cleaned, or board on time with conditions
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a medical log count ahead of the guest letter, a deck or meal common to the first cases, a crew member who worked while ill, a laboratory result, the time left before the 24-hour report point
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a satellite link that fails during the report window, a medical log kept on paper in two places, a cleaning crew short of disinfectant, a port agent who cannot reach the quarantine station
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the CDC Vessel Sanitation Program and the port health authority
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: State counts as cases of persons on board, with passengers and crew separate, and compute percentages from the persons on board. Counts are cumulative for the voyage and never go down. Time reports against arrival (24 to 36 hours before, and 4 hours before). Use the reportable case definition only in the medical-log context. Give hygiene and isolation steps from cited guidance and no medical advice beyond it. The ship, the line and the port are fictional.

decisionMustMention.description: the CDC, the port health authority or the quarantine station

addedThreatFamilies.label: Hurricane affecting a resort or an itinerary
addedThreatFamilies.description: A tropical cyclone threatens a resort or a ship's itinerary; guest departures depend on flight and road clearance, and the front office must account for every guest.

phaseArc.title: Watch
phaseArc.goal: The advisory cone includes the property or a port; guests ask whether to leave.
beats: A tropical storm watch is issued for the coast
Airlines publish waivers
The ship's routing office offers a new track

phaseArc.title: Departure window
phaseArc.goal: Flight and road clearance set how many guests can leave and when.
beats: Roads to the airport begin to close
Departures lag the plan
Staff ask about their own families

phaseArc.title: Shelter in place
phaseArc.goal: Remaining guests move to the shelter plan and the front office tracks every room.
beats: Elevators are locked out
Power is on generator
A guest with a medical need needs help

phaseArc.title: Impact and accounting
phaseArc.goal: The storm passes; every guest and staff member is accounted for and damage is assessed.
beats: Two rooms do not answer
Guests ask when they can leave
Insurers and brands ask for status

phaseArc.title: Recovery and return
phaseArc.goal: Reopening, rebooking and guest communications.
beats: The airport reopens in stages
Refund and rebooking questions arrive

decisionPointExamples: close the resort to new arrivals now, or keep selling the weekend until the next advisory
order the last departure convoy before the road floods, or hold guests in place
send the ship around the storm and cancel a port, or hold the port call and risk the weather
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: an advisory time that moved the cone, a road closure notice, an airline waiver, a guest list that does not match the rooms occupied, a generator fuel level
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a flight cancellation that strands guests, a shuttle driver who will not drive, a power loss that locks keycards, a phone system that fails
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: county emergency management and the airline and ground transport partners
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Tie each action to an advisory time and a departure window, not to the clock alone. Use the property's own floors and room counts. Guests are counted by name or room code and never by real personal data.

decisionMustMention.description: county emergency management, the airline or the port

addedThreatFamilies.label: Guest death, serious injury or missing person
addedThreatFamilies.description: A guest dies, is seriously hurt, goes missing or is lost overboard; notifications to families, authorities and consulates run beside operations and media interest.

phaseArc.title: The report
phaseArc.goal: A crew member reports the event; the first minutes decide who is told.
beats: A cabin steward finds a guest unresponsive
A camera shows a person entering the water
A family reports a guest missing

phaseArc.title: Immediate response
phaseArc.goal: Medical response, search and scene protection start together.
beats: The ship turns and starts a search plan
Security secures the cabin
The doctor declares death

phaseArc.title: Notifications
phaseArc.goal: Authorities, family, consulate and the company are told in order.
beats: The FBI and Coast Guard report is due
The family is reached by phone
The consulate asks for a manifest line

phaseArc.title: Communication
phaseArc.goal: Media and social posts begin before the facts are complete.
beats: A passenger posts a video
A reporter calls the shoreside team
Staff ask what they may say

phaseArc.title: Follow-up
phaseArc.goal: Support for the family and crew, records, and the review.
beats: The coroner asks for records
Crew need support
The company reviews procedures

decisionPointExamples: call the family now with partial facts, or wait for a confirmed identification
keep searching and delay the port, or resume the itinerary
release a holding statement now, or wait for the authority to speak first
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a camera time, a muster list that is one short, a key card entry log, a family call to the hotline, a time the person was last seen
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a cabin camera with no recording, a manifest with a wrong spelling, a language barrier with the family, a consulate closed overnight
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the Coast Guard, the FBI and the family
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Keep to coordination steps and notifications. Do not describe injuries or methods of harm. Every guest, crew member and family is fictional.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Cyber attack on reservations, property management or keycards
addedThreatFamilies.description: Reservations, the property management system or keycards fail on a busy weekend; front desk, housekeeping and security run degraded and guests queue.

phaseArc.title: Detection
phaseArc.goal: Odd behavior in reservations and keycards points to an attack.
beats: The front desk cannot check in a guest
Keycards fail to encode
A ransom note appears on a back-office server

phaseArc.title: Degraded operations
phaseArc.goal: The property moves to paper check-in and manual keys.
beats: Housekeeping works from printed lists
Guests wait in the lobby
Staff ask what to tell guests

phaseArc.title: Containment and reporting
phaseArc.goal: Technical teams isolate systems and decide what to report and to whom.
beats: Guest data may be involved
The card processor asks questions
The brand asks for status

phaseArc.title: Guest and media communication
phaseArc.goal: Guests, travel agents and the press ask when service returns.
beats: A viral lobby video
A letter under every door

phaseArc.title: Recovery
phaseArc.goal: Systems return in an order that protects safety first.
beats: Keycards return before the reservation system
Reconciliation of lost bookings

decisionPointExamples: cut keycard encoding and cut keys by hand, or hold arrivals at the door
tell guests their card data may be involved now, or wait for the investigation
pay or refuse, with legal and the insurer in the room
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a failing encoder log, a locked reservations database, a duplicate booking, a vendor call, a ransom note
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: no paper forms printed in advance, a master key shortage, a call center on the same network, a backup that is also encrypted
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: the brand, the card processor and the property management vendor
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Show degraded-mode operations in detail: paper check-in, manual keys, a run list. Do not name real hotel companies, vendors or incidents. Keep attacker methods at the level of symptoms the staff see.

decisionMustMention.description: the brand, the processor, the vendor or law enforcement

addedThreatFamilies.label: Security incident in a lobby or public space
addedThreatFamilies.description: A person with a weapon, a threat call or a disturbance in a lobby; guests are moved or held, police are called and messages must be consistent.

phaseArc.title: Report
phaseArc.goal: Security receives a report and decides how to verify.
beats: A guest reports a person with a weapon
Cameras show part of the lobby
A call claims a threat

phaseArc.title: Protective action
phaseArc.goal: Staff choose between moving guests, holding in place and locking down.
beats: The front desk asks what to say
Elevators are held
A conference group is in the ballroom

phaseArc.title: Police coordination
phaseArc.goal: Police arrive and control the scene; hotel staff support.
beats: Police ask for a floor plan and a master key
Staff count guests in the area

phaseArc.title: Communication
phaseArc.goal: Guests, families and the press ask for facts.
beats: A social post claims shots were fired
The brand asks for a statement

phaseArc.title: Reunification and review
phaseArc.goal: Guests return to rooms, staff are supported and the review begins.
beats: A guest asks about a missing family member
A debrief is scheduled

decisionPointExamples: hold guests in place, or move them away from the lobby through a service corridor
lock down the tower, or keep elevators running for people already on their way out
release a statement before police confirm, or wait
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a camera still, a door log, a call recording, a staff member who saw the person, a guest list for the area
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a master key not at the desk, a floor plan out of date, a PA system with no hotel-wide zone, a radio dead zone in the garage
addedThreatFamilies.keyCoordination: police and the property's emergency management partners
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Coordination-level detail only. Do not describe weapons, tactics or methods. Staff roles, guest movement, communication and the police handoff are the content. All people are fictional.

addedThreatFamilies.label: Fire or life-safety event in a hotel tower
addedThreatFamilies.description: A fire alarm or fire on a floor of a hotel tower; guests on upper floors, mobility needs, accounting by floor and information to the fire department.

phaseArc.title: Alarm
phaseArc.goal: The panel shows a device on a floor and staff decide what to do.
beats: Front office sees an alarm on floor 14
A guest calls about smoke
Engineering goes to check

phaseArc.title: Evacuation and accounting
phaseArc.goal: Floors are cleared and guests accounted for against the in-house list.
beats: Guests with mobility needs are on upper floors
Stairwells fill
The list is out of date

phaseArc.title: Fire department coordination
phaseArc.goal: Command takes over; staff supply keys, plans and counts.
beats: The fire department asks which rooms are unaccounted
Elevators are recalled

phaseArc.title: Care and information
phaseArc.goal: Displaced guests need rooms, medicine and information.
beats: Guests stand in the street
A family asks about a missing child

phaseArc.title: Recovery
phaseArc.goal: Floors are reoccupied or closed; the review begins.
beats: A floor stays closed
Insurers ask for the timeline

decisionPointExamples: re-enter a floor to check rooms, or hold for the fire department
move displaced guests to another property, or shelter them in the ballroom
use the in-house list as printed, or the front desk's live view
addedThreatFamilies.clueKinds: a panel device address, a guest call, an in-house list with a printout time, a floor warden report
addedThreatFamilies.hurdleKinds: a printout older than the live list, a stairwell door that locks, an elevator out of service, a language barrier on a floor
addedThreatFamilies.promptGuidance: Account by floor and room with the time of the list. Keep to evacuation, accounting and information. Do not describe fire behavior or methods.

a cabin steward asking about a broken shower
a shore excursion operator confirming a pickup time
